# Bunki L2B.0 grammar manifest draft

Status: **draft, not independently reviewed, not frozen, not complete for presentation**.

This packet enumerates 240 canonical authored N5–N1 patterns and all 289 AI-written N1/N2 records at base commit `65f84d7ff6b308ad9ebbecea0bcdbef492c44daa`. It preserves 533 source records as 529 units: four harvested aliases attach to their inline corridor winners. The 144 cross-family same-pattern candidates remain separate pending native disambiguation; text equality never merges identities.

Every unit carries its actual source meaning, formation, register/usage field (null where the source lacks it), contrasts where present, examples, source-example links, draft outcome, prerequisite, assessment obligation, review obligations, and required work. The N5→N1 sequence follows the existing `mergeGrammar` convention and keeps stable source order within each family. Its prerequisites are editorial sequencing proposals, not learner history or claims of linguistic dependency.

## Boundaries and open coverage

- No entry is marked native-reviewed. The 289 generated records retain their AI-created/AI-reviewed, native-unconfirmed provenance; translation-faithfulness evidence is not native grammar review.
- Authored entries currently have one or two examples, so every one needs at least one more before S2-R23 completion. Generated records already have three.
- G9 is present at the requested base. MF1@data, MF2@data, and a durable first-full-version reading occurrence inventory are not available in this checkout. Their constructions must be mapped or added before MF4R/MF4; this packet does not claim that coverage denominator is closed.
- Source-example links are not substitutes for occurrence reconciliation across the on-ramp, readings, and kanji units. No substring matcher is used to invent occurrence links.
- No learner history, scheduling event, campaign file, receipt, runbook, credential, or native iPhone artifact is read or written by the generator.

## Reproduce and validate

From this directory, with Node.js 22.13 or newer:

```sh
node build.mjs
node validate.mjs
node validate.mjs --self-test
```

The following fenced JSON is the manifest data consumed by validation and intended for the later freeze step. It is not a frozen hash or an MF4 output.

      "formation": "Vた形 / イAい / ナAな + ことに",

        },

          "cloze": "うれしいことに"

      "formation": "N / 普通形 + というと／といえば／といったら",

      "examples": [

          "cloze": "といったら"

      "register": "Attaches to verbs of perceiving or thinking (見る, 聞く, 思う) and is followed by a feeling or recollection that arises naturally; somewhat literary. Also survives in set phrases such as 何かにつけて (at every turn) and 良きにつけ悪しきにつけ (for better or worse).",

      "level": "N2",
      "meaning": {
        "en": "despite …; in spite of …; even though …",
        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "普通形 + にもかかわらず（なA語幹・N は そのまま／である）/ N + にもかかわらず",
      "register": "A formal, written-leaning 'despite' that presents an outcome running against what the first fact would lead one to expect, often with surprise or mild criticism. The second clause cannot be a command, request or intention; also used sentence-initially as それにもかかわらず.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜のに: conversational and more emotional (complaint, regret); にもかかわらず is more objective and formal",
        "〜ものの: concedes the first fact before a softer contrast ('although')",
        "〜にかかわらず (no も): 'regardless of' (天候にかかわらず), a completely different meaning"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-58ea79ffc5a3:example:1",
          "ja": "平日の朝にもかかわらず、新しいカフェの前には長い行列ができていた。",
          "en": "Even though it was a weekday morning, there was a long line outside the new café.",
          "cloze": "朝にもかかわらず"

          "ja": "再三の注意喚起があったにもかかわらず、山での遭難事故は今年も後を絶たない。",
          "en": "Despite repeated warnings, there has again been no end to mountain accidents this year.",
          "cloze": "あったにもかかわらず"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-58ea79ffc5a3:example:3",
          "ja": "あいにくの雨にもかかわらず、大勢のファンがスタジアムに駆けつけてくれた。",
          "en": "In spite of the unfortunate rain, a huge number of fans turned out at the stadium for us.",
          "cloze": "雨にもかかわらず"
        }

      "level": "N2",
      "meaning": {
        "en": "as …, gradually …; in proportion as …",
        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "V辞書形 / N + につれ(て)",
      "register": "Describes proportional change: as one thing changes, another changes along with it step by step. Both clauses express a gradual change, so it does not suit one-off events or a request or intention in the second clause.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜に伴って: more formal, and can link a single event to its consequence (移転に伴い); につれて needs ongoing, gradual change",
        "〜にしたがって: nearly the same for proportional change, but can also mean 'in accordance with' rules or instructions",
        "〜とともに: broader 'along with / at the same time as', including simple coincidence or 'together with a person'"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-6ed1904bcf0a:example:1",
          "ja": "日が暮れるにつれて、通りの人出はますます増えていった。",
          "en": "As the sun went down, the streets grew more and more crowded.",
          "cloze": "暮れるにつれて"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-6ed1904bcf0a:example:2",
          "ja": "年齢を重ねるにつれて、若い頃には分からなかった親の苦労が見えてきた。",
          "en": "As I've grown older, I've come to see the hardships my parents went through that I couldn't understand when I was young.",
          "cloze": "重ねるにつれて"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-6ed1904bcf0a:example:3",
          "ja": "円安が進むにつれ、海外からの観光客が急増している。",
          "en": "As the yen continues to weaken, the number of tourists from abroad is surging.",
          "cloze": "進むにつれ"
        }
      ],

      "register": "Used with nouns like 予想, 期待, 意思 or 規則 to say a result went the opposite way from expectations, or that an act goes against a rule or someone's will. Formal; common in news and sports reporting.",

        "〜に背いて: 'defying / disobeying', a stronger, more deliberate act"

      },
      "formation": "N / Naな / Aい / V普通形 + だけに",
      "register": "Two uses: 'as you would expect given …', fairly neutral and fine for bad results, and 'all the more because …', where the reason intensifies the result, often disappointment or relief. Common in news and essays, sometimes reinforced as だけになおさら.",

          "cloze": "だけに"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-7d2c48cca169:example:3",
          "ja": "初めての海外出張だっただけに、無事に契約がまとまったときは本当にほっとした。",
          "en": "Since it was my first overseas business trip, I was all the more relieved when the contract was safely concluded.",
          "cloze": "だけに"
        }
      ],

      },
      "formation": "N + に限って",
      "register": "Mostly used with frustration: something bad happens at exactly the worst moment (急いでいる時に限って). With a negative, it expresses trust that a particular person would never do something (うちの子に限って…ない).",

      "register": "Used with nouns like 期待, 要望, 声援 or 拍手: someone acts to meet the expectations, wishes or cheers of others. Positive in tone and fairly formal.",

        "〜を受けて: 'in light of / following' an event, a neutral cause"

      "examples": [

          "cloze": "拍手に応えて"
        }

      ],
      "examples": [

          "cloze": "知っているかのような"

      "draftVersion": 1,
      "family": "generated",
      "pattern": "〜ならまだしも",
      "level": "N1",
      "meaning": {
        "en": "… would be one thing, but …; … might be acceptable, but …",
        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "N / 普通形 + ならまだしも",
      "register": "Concedes that a lesser case could be tolerated, then complains that the real situation is worse. Used in speech and writing; the speaker is clearly dissatisfied.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜ならいざ知らず: same frame but more formal and literary",
        "〜ならともかく: nearly the same, slightly less emphatic",
        "〜はともかく: neutral 'setting aside', no complaint built in"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-0e09d6a166be:example:1",
          "ja": "一度ならまだしも、毎週のように遅刻されては困る。",
          "en": "Once would be one thing, but being late practically every week is a problem.",
          "cloze": "ならまだしも"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-0e09d6a166be:example:2",
          "ja": "値段が高いだけならまだしも、品質まで落ちたのでは客離れも当然だ。",
          "en": "Being expensive would be one thing, but with the quality dropping too, it is no wonder customers are leaving.",
          "cloze": "ならまだしも"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-0e09d6a166be:example:3",
          "ja": "冗談で言ったのならまだしも、本気でそう考えているなら問題だ。",
          "en": "If it was said as a joke, fine, but if they really think that, it's a problem.",
          "cloze": "ならまだしも"
        }
      ],

      "meaning": {

        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "ナ形容詞語幹 + 極まりない / 極まる；イ形容詞い・ナ形容詞な + こと + 極まりない（例: 危険極まりない、失礼極まる、腹立たしいこと極まりない）",
      "register": "A formal, emphatic way to condemn something, mostly with negative na-adjectives such as 失礼, 危険, 迷惑, 不愉快 and 退屈. Common in news, editorials and angry complaints; 〜極まる means the same but sounds more literary.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜の極み: 'the height of', attaches to nouns (感激の極み, 贅沢の極み) and can be positive",

        "〜限りだ: voices the speaker's own feeling (嬉しい限りだ) rather than a judgment of something"

      "examples": [

          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-11ed0bafc92f:example:1",

          "cloze": "危険極まりない"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-11ed0bafc92f:example:2",
          "ja": "予約の時間に一時間も遅れておきながら謝罪の一言もないとは、失礼極まりない。",
          "en": "Turning up an hour late for the reservation without a single word of apology is the height of rudeness.",
          "cloze": "失礼極まりない"
        },

          "en": "At the post-match press conference, the manager sharply criticized the referees, calling it an utterly baffling decision.",
          "cloze": "不可解極まる"
        }

      "id": "gram:generated:nsrs-g-13a260e8b08b",

      "meaning": {

        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "Vて形 + からというもの",
      "register": "Marks a turning point after which the situation has changed and stayed changed; the speaker looks back with feeling at how different things have been since. Literary and emotional, so it rarely appears with routine events.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜て以来: neutral 'since'; てからというもの stresses a striking, lasting change and carries more feeling",
        "〜てから: plain 'after'; no sense of a continuing changed state",
        "〜を境に: 'with … as a turning point', also used for one-off shifts and in reports"
      ],
      "examples": [

          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-13a260e8b08b:example:1",

          "en": "Ever since I started working from home, the fatigue of commuting has gone and I can make good use of my mornings.",

        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-13a260e8b08b:example:2",

          "en": "Ever since a big shopping mall opened in front of the station, foot traffic in the shopping street has dropped sharply.",
          "cloze": "できてからというもの"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-13a260e8b08b:example:3",
          "ja": "子どもが生まれてからというもの、夜にゆっくり映画を見たことなど一度もない。",
          "en": "Ever since our child was born, I haven't once sat back and watched a movie at night.",
          "cloze": "生まれてからというもの"
        }

      "formation": "N + によらず",
      "register": "Formal, common in policies, recruitment and official notices (年齢によらず, 国籍によらず). Also appears in set phrases: 見かけによらず ('contrary to appearances') and 何事によらず ('whatever it may be').",

        "〜もかまわず: heedless of, describing someone's behaviour ignoring something"

      "meaning": {

        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "V普通形 / Vない形 + こととて ; Aな語幹 + な + こととて ; Nの + こととて",
      "register": "An old-fashioned, formal causal used to offer a reason when apologising or asking for forgiveness. Found in letters, business apologies and polite speech; the main clause is often an apology or request for leniency.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜ゆえ(に): formal 'because' with no apologetic nuance",
        "〜ので: plain, everyday 'because'",
        "〜ことだから: reason based on knowing someone's character (あの人のことだから)"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-28d24e11a628:example:1",
          "ja": "何分にも慣れないこととて、ご迷惑をおかけしましたことを深くお詫び申し上げます。",
          "en": "As we were entirely unaccustomed to this, we deeply apologise for the inconvenience caused.",
          "cloze": "慣れないこととて"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-28d24e11a628:example:2",
          "ja": "急なこととて、十分なおもてなしもできず失礼いたしました。",
          "en": "As it was so sudden, please forgive us for not being able to welcome you properly.",
          "cloze": "急なこととて"
        },

      "family": "generated",
      "pattern": "〜かたわら",
      "level": "N1",
      "meaning": {
        "en": "while also …; alongside (one's main work) …",
        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "V辞書形 / Nの + かたわら",
      "register": "Someone pursues a second activity alongside their main occupation over a long period. Written and slightly literary, common in profiles and biographies; it also has the literal sense 'beside'.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜ながら: two activities in parallel, either at a particular moment or over a longer period (働きながら大学に通う); everyday register",
        "〜一方(で): contrasting two aspects or activities, not necessarily main versus side",
        "〜かたがた: one action serving two purposes on a single occasion"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-31c3bd04df13:example:1",
          "ja": "その作家は、会社勤めのかたわら、毎朝欠かさず小説を書き続けた。",
          "en": "Alongside a day job at a company, the writer kept writing fiction every morning without fail.",
          "cloze": "会社勤めのかたわら"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-31c3bd04df13:example:2",
          "ja": "彼女は大学で研究を続けるかたわら、地域の子どもたちに無料で勉強を教えている。",
          "en": "Alongside her research at a university, she tutors local children for free.",
          "cloze": "続けるかたわら"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-31c3bd04df13:example:3",
          "ja": "農業を営むかたわら、古民家を改装したカフェを経営する人が増えている。",
          "en": "More and more people are running cafés in renovated old houses while also working as farmers.",
          "cloze": "営むかたわら"
        }
      ],

      "examples": [

      },
      "formation": "V辞書形 + や否や / や",
      "register": "Shows that a second event follows the first almost instantly. Written and formal, typical of news and narrative; the second clause describes what actually happened, never a request or intention, and the short form 〜や is even more literary.",

        "〜なり: 'as soon as', same subject, often a sudden or unusual action",
        "〜が早いか: 'no sooner than', literary and nearly identical in meaning"
      ],
      "examples": [

          "ja": "ベルが鳴るや否や、生徒たちは教室を飛び出していった。",
          "en": "The moment the bell rang, the students rushed out of the classroom.",

        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-365be68c80ea:example:3",

          "en": "As soon as they heard about the accident, the reporters all headed to the scene.",
          "cloze": "聞くや"
        }

      "meaning": {

      },
      "formation": "V辞書形 + に足る + N / N(する名詞) + に足る + N",
      "register": "Formal, usually attributive: something is adequate or worthy enough to justify an action or judgment (信頼に足る, 尊敬に足る, 証明するに足る). The negative idiom 取るに足らない means 'trivial'.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜に値する: deserves, stressing merit or value (賞賛に値する)",
        "〜に堪える: able to stand up to use or scrutiny",
        "〜に足りない: insufficient or not worthy of; 取るに足らない is the idiom meaning 'trivial / not worth bothering with'"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-37803fb3532a:example:1",
          "ja": "投資家に対して信頼に足る情報を開示できなければ、資金は集まらない。",
          "en": "If you can't disclose information that investors can trust, you won't raise any money.",
          "cloze": "信頼に足る"
        },

          "ja": "現時点では、その説を裏付けるに足る証拠は見つかっていない。",
          "en": "So far, no evidence sufficient to support that theory has been found.",
          "cloze": "裏付けるに足る"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-37803fb3532a:example:3",
          "ja": "家族を養うに足る収入を得るのは、この業界では簡単ではない。",
          "en": "Earning enough to support a family is not easy in this industry.",
          "cloze": "養うに足る"
        }

      "id": "gram:generated:nsrs-g-399434e8ed0d",
      "draftVersion": 1,
      "family": "generated",
      "pattern": "〜もかまわず",
      "level": "N1",
      "meaning": {
        "en": "heedless of …; without caring about …",
        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "N + もかまわず; V・イA普通形 / ナA・N + な + の + もかまわず",
      "register": "Describes someone acting without regard for something they would normally worry about, such as other people's eyes, the weather or the hour. Often carries mild criticism or surprise from the speaker.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜をよそに: 'paying no heed to', usually others' worries or opposition; more written",
        "〜にかまわず: same meaning with a different particle; also used as a request (私にかまわず)",
        "〜を問わず: 'regardless of', neutral, with no sense of disregard"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-399434e8ed0d:example:1",
          "ja": "その子は服が汚れるのもかまわず、水たまりで遊び続けた。",
          "en": "The child kept playing in the puddle without caring that their clothes were getting dirty.",
          "cloze": "汚れるのもかまわず"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-399434e8ed0d:example:2",
          "ja": "人目もかまわず、駅のホームで大声で泣いている人がいた。",
          "en": "Someone was crying loudly on the station platform, heedless of who was watching.",
          "cloze": "人目もかまわず"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-399434e8ed0d:example:3",
          "ja": "隣の住人は深夜なのもかまわず、大音量で音楽を流している。",
          "en": "The neighbour plays music at full volume, without caring that it's the middle of the night.",
          "cloze": "深夜なのもかまわず"
        }
      ],

      "draftVersion": 1,

      "pattern": "〜がましい",
      "level": "N1",
      "meaning": {
        "en": "smacking of …; coming across unpleasantly as … (disapproved)",
        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "N / Vます形 + がましい (恩着せがましい・言い訳がましい・押し付けがましい・差し出がましい)",
      "register": "Attaches to a limited set of words to say that someone's words or manner come across unpleasantly as that thing: excuse-making, favour-flaunting, pushy or clinging (言い訳がましい, 恩着せがましい, 押し付けがましい, 未練がましい). Almost always critical; 差し出がましいようですが is a set humble opener before giving advice.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜じみる: looks or feels like something it should not be (子供じみた, 所帯じみた); about resemblance, not off-putting behaviour aimed at others",
        "〜っぽい: casual '-ish', often neutral; no sense of imposing on others",
        "〜らしい: 'typical of / befitting'; usually neutral or positive"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-39d5971dc404:example:1",
          "ja": "手伝ってくれたのはありがたいが、あんなに恩着せがましく言われると素直に喜べない。",
          "en": "I'm grateful for the help, but when they make such a point of how much I owe them, I can't feel properly pleased about it.",
          "cloze": "恩着せがましく"
        },
        {

          "ja": "遅刻の理由を長々と説明すると、かえって言い訳がましく聞こえる。",
          "en": "If you go on at length about why you were late, it just sounds like you're making excuses.",
          "cloze": "言い訳がましく"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-39d5971dc404:example:3",
          "ja": "差し出がましいようですが、その資料は先に部長に見せた方がいいと思います。",
          "en": "I hope I'm not overstepping, but I think you should show those materials to the department head first.",
          "cloze": "差し出がましい"
        }
      ],

      "formation": "Vない形 + ずして (する → せずして)",
      "register": "A literary, formal way of saying 'without doing', heard mostly in set phrases such as 労せずして, 戦わずして and 期せずして, and in the frame 〜ずして〜ない ('without doing X, one cannot Y'). It belongs to written commentary, speeches and headlines rather than casual talk.",

        "〜ことなく: formal 'without ever …', stressing that the action never takes place"
      ],
      "examples": [

      "register": "Classical equivalents of ような / ように, used in formal writing, speeches and set phrases such as 前述のごとく. Attached directly to a person noun (私ごとき, あなたごとき) it becomes humble or contemptuous.",

      "examples": [

        },

      ],
      "examples": [

          "cloze": "は言うに及ばず"

        },
        {

        }

      "register": "Classical prohibition, seen today on signs, notices and in proverbs (立ち入るべからず). べからざる modifies a noun in set phrases such as 欠くべからざる ('indispensable') and 許すべからざる ('unforgivable').",

          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-3f7a9e81b3b3:example:3",
          "ja": "「働かざる者食うべからず」という言葉を、祖父はよく口にしていた。",

          "cloze": "食うべからず"
        }

      "register": "A literary, formal equivalent of 〜なくても, often followed by わかる, いい or 構わない, with 言わずとも as the most familiar set phrase. With nouns it appears as ならずとも ('even if not …'), as in 専門家ならずとも.",

      ],
      "examples": [

      "register": "Concedes or affirms one thing in order to firmly deny the other; こそすれ is usually followed by a negative, as in 'one might X, but never Y'. Formal and written; set phrases include 程度の差こそあれ and 感謝こそすれ.",
      "contrasts": [

        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-5f8490f471ca:example:3",
          "ja": "今回の規制緩和は、地方の小売店にとって打撃になりこそすれ、追い風にはならないだろう。",

      "register": "A literary particle surviving mainly in fixed expressions: 考えるだに恐ろしい, 想像するだに, 微動だにしない, 一顧だにしない. It stresses that even the slightest act triggers a feeling, or that not even the minimum happens.",

      "examples": [

          "cloze": "一顧だに"

      "meaning": {

        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "N / V辞書形 + こと + はおろか（後に も・さえ・すら・まで）",
      "register": "Names the case where the statement obviously holds first, then a more basic or extreme one marked by も, さえ or すら ('not even B, let alone A'), usually in a negative sentence. Carries surprise or exasperation, so it is not used with requests, commands or the speaker's intentions.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜どころか: more conversational, and can also flip expectations ('far from X, actually Y')",
        "〜ばかりか: neutral 'not only', positive or negative",
        "〜はもちろん: neutral 'of course X, and Y too', without the exasperated tone"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-619e974d499f:example:1",
          "ja": "入社して三か月、ボーナスはおろか、まともな残業代すら支払われていない。",
          "en": "Three months after joining the company, I haven't even been paid proper overtime, let alone a bonus.",
          "cloze": "はおろか"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-619e974d499f:example:2",
          "ja": "その村には、コンビニはおろか信号機さえ一つもない。",
          "en": "That village doesn't have a single traffic light, let alone a convenience store.",
          "cloze": "はおろか"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-619e974d499f:example:3",
          "ja": "足を骨折してしまい、走ることはおろか、一人で歩くこともできない。",
          "en": "I broke my leg and can't even walk on my own, let alone run.",
          "cloze": "はおろか"
        }
      ],

      },
      "formation": "N + をもって（丁寧：をもちまして）",
      "register": "A formal replacement for で, used for the means or quality with which something is done and for the point at which something ends. Typical of announcements, official notices and speeches; in daily conversation it sounds stiff.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜で: the everyday particle for means and time limits, with no formality",
        "〜を限りに: stresses that something ongoing stops after this point, often a personal decision",
        "〜をもってすれば: praises a means that makes something possible, not just names it"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-65eacdc75fd3:example:1",
          "ja": "当店は今月末をもって閉店いたします。長年のご愛顧、誠にありがとうございました。",
          "en": "Our shop will close at the end of this month. Thank you very much for your many years of patronage.",
          "cloze": "をもって"

      "level": "N1",
      "meaning": {
        "en": "… aside, but …; it may be different for …, but …",
        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "N / 普通形 + ならいざ知らず（N + はいざ知らず）",
      "register": "Formal and somewhat literary. Grants that an exceptional case might be excused or different, then holds the actual case to a stricter standard; usually critical or surprised.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜ならまだしも: 'X would be tolerable, but'; more conversational and openly complaining",

        "〜ならともかく: close in meaning, less formal"
      ],
      "examples": [

          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-6f063f4a2fcd:example:1",
          "ja": "子どもならいざ知らず、大人がこんな簡単なルールも守れないとは情けない。",
          "en": "A child would be one thing, but it is pathetic that adults can't follow even such a simple rule.",
          "cloze": "ならいざ知らず"

        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-6f063f4a2fcd:example:2",
          "ja": "昔はいざ知らず、今はスマホ一台で世界中の情報が手に入る。",
          "en": "The past may have been different, but now you can get information from all over the world with a single smartphone.",
          "cloze": "はいざ知らず"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-6f063f4a2fcd:example:3",
          "ja": "個人の趣味ならいざ知らず、税金を使う事業である以上、説明責任は免れない。",
          "en": "If it were a personal hobby, perhaps, but since this project uses taxpayers' money, there is no escaping accountability.",
          "cloze": "ならいざ知らず"
        }
      ],

      },
      "formation": "N(+助詞) + すら ; Nで + すら ; Vます形 + すら + しない",

          "cloze": "名前すら"
        }

      "draftVersion": 1,

      "meaning": {

        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "V辞書形 + には当たらない / N(する名詞) + には当たらない",
      "register": "Formal and evaluative: the speaker calmly judges that a reaction such as surprise, alarm, praise or blame is not called for. Typical partners are 驚く, 悲観する, 嘆く, 非難する, 賞賛する; common in commentary, editorials and expert remarks.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜までもない: no need because it is too obvious or trivial to bother; には当たらない says the reaction itself is unwarranted",
        "〜には及ばない: no need to go to that trouble (often a polite 'don't bother'), or 'is no match for'",
        "〜ことはない: everyday 'there's no need to', reassuring and conversational"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-9abbdf468a0d:example:1",
          "ja": "新人が初戦で負けたからといって、悲観するには当たらない。",
          "en": "Just because the rookie lost the first match, there is no reason to be pessimistic.",
          "cloze": "悲観するには当たらない"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-9abbdf468a0d:example:2",
          "ja": "この程度の値上がりは過去にも何度もあり、驚くには当たらないと専門家は話す。",
          "en": "Experts say price rises of this size have happened many times before and are nothing to be surprised about.",
          "cloze": "驚くには当たらない"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-9abbdf468a0d:example:3",
          "ja": "店員の対応は規則どおりで、非難には当たらないというのが会社の見解だ。",
          "en": "The company's position is that the clerk acted according to the rules and does not deserve criticism.",
          "cloze": "非難には当たらない"
        }
      ],

      "meaning": {

      "formation": "V辞書形 + べくもない（する → すべくもない）",
      "register": "Formal, written; states that something is out of the question, often about the gap between a hope and reality. Common with 望む, 知る, 比べる, 疑う.",

          "cloze": "望むべくもなかった"

          "cloze": "比べるべくもない"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-a2bcf4a52a0a:example:3",
          "ja": "百年前に失われたその手紙に何が書かれていたのか、今となっては知るべくもない。",
          "en": "There is no way now of knowing what was written in that letter, lost a hundred years ago.",
          "cloze": "知るべくもない"
        }
      ],

      "meaning": {

      },
      "formation": "N（人・組織）+ をして + V使役形（〜させる / 〜しめる）",
      "register": "A literary causative that marks who is made to act, typically when something is so striking that even that person reacts. Found in formal writing and reviews, often with 言わしめる.",

      ],
      "examples": [

          "cloze": "学界をして"
        },
        {

          "ja": "その絶景は、旅慣れた人をして思わず言葉を失わせるほどだ。",
          "en": "The view is so spectacular that it leaves even seasoned travellers speechless.",
          "cloze": "人をして"
        }

      "meaning": {

        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "N + ときたら",
      "register": "Conversational. Raises a topic close to the speaker (family, colleagues, a familiar thing) in order to complain about it; the comment that follows is almost always negative or exasperated.",

      "examples": [

          "cloze": "ときたら"

      "meaning": {
        "en": "without …; (with a following negative) cannot … without …",
        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "N + なしに（は）/ V辞書形 + ことなしに（は）",
      "register": "Somewhat formal, though set phrases like 予告なしに or 断りなしに are common in speech. Plain なしに means 'without X / without doing'; なしには is followed by a negative or impossibility to say X is an indispensable condition.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜ことなく: 'without doing', attaches to verbs only and does not imply a condition",
        "〜抜きで / 抜きには: 'leaving X out'; more conversational",
        "〜なくして（は）: even more literary near-synonym of なしには, almost always followed by a negative"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-ae30b4388971:example:1",
          "ja": "住民の理解なしには、この再開発計画を進めることはできない。",
          "en": "This redevelopment plan cannot go forward without the residents' understanding.",
          "cloze": "なしには"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-ae30b4388971:example:2",
          "ja": "上司への報告もなしに新人が契約を結んでしまい、社内は大騒ぎになった。",
          "en": "A new hire signed the contract without even reporting to their boss, and the office was thrown into an uproar.",
          "cloze": "なしに"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-ae30b4388971:example:3",
          "ja": "努力することなしに夢をかなえた人など、ほとんどいないだろう。",
          "en": "There are probably very few people who have achieved their dreams without making an effort.",
          "cloze": "することなしに"
        }
      ],

      "family": "generated",
      "pattern": "〜ずにはおかない",
      "level": "N1",
      "meaning": {
        "en": "cannot fail to (cause); will inevitably …; will definitely … (strong resolve)",
        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "Vない形 + ずにはおかない (する → せずにはおかない); also Vない形 + ないではおかない",
      "register": "A formal, assertive expression with two uses: something naturally and inevitably provokes a reaction (often with a causative, as in 感動させずにはおかない), or someone is firmly determined to do something. Common in reviews, editorials and official statements.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜ずにはいられない: the speaker cannot hold back their own urge; ずにはおかない is about a thing that inevitably causes a reaction, or a firm will",
        "〜ずにはすまない: an obligation that circumstances or social norms make unavoidable",
        "〜ないではおかない: the same meaning in a slightly less literary form"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-afe064a96b62:example:1",
          "ja": "被災地の人々の力強い言葉は、聞く者の心を動かさずにはおかない。",
          "en": "The powerful words of the people in the disaster area cannot fail to move those who hear them.",
          "cloze": "動かさずにはおかない"

        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-afe064a96b62:example:2",
          "ja": "この映画の衝撃的な結末は、観客を考え込ませずにはおかないだろう。",
          "en": "The film's shocking ending is bound to leave audiences deep in thought.",
          "cloze": "考え込ませずにはおかない"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-afe064a96b62:example:3",
          "ja": "委員会は、不正に関わった者には相応の責任を取らせずにはおかない構えだ。",
          "en": "The committee is determined to make everyone involved in the wrongdoing take due responsibility.",
          "cloze": "取らせずにはおかない"
        }

      "draftVersion": 1,
      "family": "generated",
      "pattern": "〜ばそれまでだ",
      "level": "N1",
      "meaning": {
        "en": "if …, it is all over; once …, that's the end of it",
        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "Vば（Vなければ・Vてしまえば を含む） / Aければ + それまでだ",
      "register": "Says that one event makes everything else pointless, often after a concessive どんなに or せっかく. Tone is resigned or cautionary, frequently used to warn or to justify a precaution.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜たらおしまいだ: casual spoken equivalent",
        "〜ばいい: looks similar but means 'all you have to do is'; a suggestion, not resignation",
        "〜までだ: 'I'll just …' (resolve) or 'it was merely …', not 'it's all over'"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {

      "register": "Written and narrative. V辞書形 + なり describes a sudden, often surprising action right after another by the same third-person subject; not used for the speaker's own plans, commands or the future. Vたなり means a state has continued unchanged since then.",

      "level": "N1",
      "meaning": {

        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "Vた形 + ところで (often with いくら / どんなに / 今さら, followed by a negative or minimising judgement)",
      "register": "The speaker judges that even doing something will not change the outcome, or that its effect would be small. The tone is resigned or dismissive, and the main clause is negative or minimising (〜ない, 無駄だ, せいぜい).",

        "〜ても: neutral 'even if', with no sense of futility",

        "〜たところ: 'when I did …, (I found that)', a completely different meaning"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-e2bec57185aa:example:1",

          "cloze": "急いだところで"

          "cloze": "説明したところで"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-e2bec57185aa:example:3",
          "ja": "多少値上がりしたところで、せいぜい数十円程度なので、家計への影響は小さい。",
          "en": "Even if prices go up a little, it will only be by a few dozen yen at most, so the effect on household budgets will be small.",
          "cloze": "値上がりしたところで"
        }

      "formation": "N + をおいて + ほかに〜ない / ほかにいない",
      "register": "Singles out one person, place or moment as the only fitting choice, usually as high praise or strong urging. Formal, used in speeches, editorials and recommendations.",

        "〜を除いて: 'except for', neutral exclusion",

      "examples": [

          "ja": "日本の伝統工芸を学ぶなら、京都をおいてほかにないだろう。",

      "draftVersion": 1,
      "family": "generated",
      "pattern": "〜かたがた",
      "level": "N1",
      "meaning": {
        "en": "combining … with …; while also (doing) …",
        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "N + かたがた (お礼 / ご挨拶 / ご報告 / お見舞い など)",
      "register": "One occasion serves two purposes: the noun before かたがた names one, and the main verb (often 伺う, 訪ねる, 申し上げる) the other. Formal and fixed, found mostly in letters and business visits with a small set of nouns.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜がてら: 'while I'm at it', less stiff and usually with going out (散歩がてら); かたがた sounds out of place in casual errands",
        "〜かたわら: pursuing two activities in parallel over a long period (job and side work)",
        "〜ついでに: incidental 'taking the opportunity', everyday register"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-ebd7db8cc3f7:example:1",
          "ja": "先日のお礼かたがた、近いうちにご挨拶に伺いたいと存じます。",
          "en": "I would like to call on you soon to pay my respects and thank you for the other day.",
          "cloze": "お礼かたがた"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-ebd7db8cc3f7:example:2",
          "ja": "略儀ながら、書中にてご報告かたがたお礼申し上げます。",
          "en": "Though it is an informal way to do so, allow me to report to you and thank you in writing.",
          "cloze": "ご報告かたがた"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-ebd7db8cc3f7:example:3",
          "ja": "入院中の恩師のお見舞いかたがた、研究の進み具合を報告しに行った。",
          "en": "I went to see my former teacher in hospital, both to wish them well and to report on how my research was going.",
          "cloze": "お見舞いかたがた"
        }
      ],

      "id": "gram:generated:nsrs-g-ec1429d4923f",
      "draftVersion": 1,
      "family": "generated",
      "pattern": "〜にもほどがある",
      "level": "N1",
      "meaning": {
        "en": "there is a limit to …; this is far too …",
        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "N / なA語幹 / いA辞書形 / V辞書形 + にもほどがある",
      "register": "Conversational and emotional: the speaker protests that something has gone beyond any acceptable limit. It carries exasperation or indignation, as in 冗談にもほどがある or 失礼にもほどがある.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜すぎる: neutral 'too much', with no indignation",
        "〜にも限度がある: near-synonym, slightly more restrained",
        "〜といったらない: extreme degree, can be positive or negative and lacks the reproach"
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-ec1429d4923f:example:1",
          "ja": "三時間も遅れてきて謝りもしないなんて、失礼にもほどがある。",

          "cloze": "失礼にもほどがある"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-ec1429d4923f:example:2",
          "ja": "ワンルームで家賃二十万円とは、強気にもほどがある。",
          "en": "Asking 200,000 yen a month for a studio apartment is pushing it way too far.",
          "cloze": "強気にもほどがある"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-ec1429d4923f:example:3",
          "ja": "人の失敗を動画にして笑いものにするなんて、ふざけるにもほどがある。",
          "en": "Filming someone's mistake and turning them into a laughingstock goes way beyond a joke.",
          "cloze": "ふざけるにもほどがある"
        }
      ],

      "meaning": {

      },
      "formation": "Vない形 + ずじまい (する → せずじまい); 〜ずじまいだ / 〜ずじまいで / 〜ずじまいになる",
      "register": "Expresses regret or disappointment that something one intended or expected never happened before the chance passed. Common in conversation and essays, often with 結局 or とうとう.",

      "examples": [

      "meaning": {

      "formation": "Vて形 / イAくて / ナA・N + であって + しかるべきだ（しかるべき + N）",
      "register": "A stiff, formal way of saying something is right and natural to expect, often used to criticise that it has not happened. Common in editorials, commentary and formal complaints.",
      "contrasts": [

        {

          "cloze": "であってしかるべきだ"

      "contrasts": [

          "en": "Regardless of the reason, fees once paid will not be refunded.",
          "cloze": "理由のいかんにかかわらず"
        },
        {
          "exampleId": "nsrs-g-f29af70c96b4:example:2",
          "ja": "試験結果のいかんによらず、参加者全員に修了証が渡される。",

          "cloze": "結果のいかんによらず"
        },
        {

          "ja": "国籍のいかんにかかわらず、誰でもこの奨学金に応募できる。",

          "cloze": "国籍のいかんにかかわらず"
        }
      ],

      "meaning": {

        "ja": null
      },
      "formation": "Nの / V普通形（Vた形・Vている形が多い）/ その + 手前",
      "register": "Says that someone, often the speaker, feels bound to keep up appearances, either in front of certain people or because of something already said or done. Usually followed by 〜わけにはいかない, 〜ざるを得ない or 〜なければならない, it carries a sense of awkward obligation and is used in both conversation and writing.",
      "contrasts": [
        "〜以上（は）: 'since, now that', a logical obligation after a clause; it never takes 'person + の' and has no idea of saving face",

        "〜上は: formal written cousin of 〜以上は, again without the 'in front of others' angle"
      ],
      "examples": [

        {
